answer: Identity verification requires a verifier-challenged chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result determining the next; GPUs can run separate chains for clones, but cannot parallelize the dependent steps of a single chain to shorten its delay. This imposes a physical time bottleneck per claimed identity, raising the cost of Sybil attacks. A Wesolowski proof lets others check the completed work efficiently, while ocean, ridge, and anchor mark distinct challenge instances.
